options: The sys_id of the most recent request for that equipment
Always true, regardless of existing requests
true if no active Approved or Checked Out request already references that equipment, false otherwise
The total count of all requests ever made for that equipment
questions.explain: gr.hasNext() checks for any matching active record in state 2 or 3; the ! negates it, so the method returns true only when no such record exists.

questions.q: Why does the Business Rule call current.setAbortAction(true) instead of just relying on the Client Script's warning?
options: setAbortAction(true) is required on every Business Rule regardless of purpose
Client-side JavaScript can be bypassed entirely (e.g. a direct API call), so only a server-side before-insert check can actually prevent a duplicate checkout
The Client Script cannot display any error message at all
Business Rules cannot run before an insert, only after
questions.explain: A Client Script is a UX convenience; the real enforcement must happen server-side where it can't be skipped, which is exactly what the before-insert Business Rule does.

questions.q: Why can't the Client Script call EquipmentAvailabilityChecker directly with GlideAjax?
options: GlideAjax cannot call any Script Include in a custom scope
EquipmentAvailabilityChecker has no methods defined
Client Scripts cannot use GlideAjax at all in scoped applications
GlideAjax can only call a Script Include that extends AbstractAjaxProcessor, which EquipmentAvailabilityChecker does not
questions.explain: That's why a separate thin wrapper, EquipmentAvailabilityCheckerAjax, extends AbstractAjaxProcessor and delegates to the real logic Script Include.

questions.q: In the ajax wrapper below, what does this.getParameter('sysparm_equipment_id') retrieve?
options: The sys_id of the current logged-in user
The value sent by the Client Script's ga.addParam('sysparm_equipment_id', newValue) call
A hardcoded equipment ID defined inside the wrapper itself
The table name the GlideAjax call is targeting
questions.explain: AbstractAjaxProcessor's getParameter() reads a parameter the client added with addParam() under the same name.

questions.q: Why does isEquipmentAvailable() use gr.hasNext() rather than gr.getRowCount() > 0?
options: hasNext() stops checking at the first matching record instead of counting every match, which matters for performance
getRowCount() is not a valid GlideRecord method
hasNext() returns a string while getRowCount() returns a number
There is no functional or performance difference between the two
questions.explain: This performance distinction is the exact kind of finding Lesson 37's code review calls out — hasNext() avoids counting every matching row just to check existence.
